description.text:
THE SEMANTIC BRIDGE (The "So What?"): The slide establishes a clear hierarchy of information, where the authoritative Adobe brand logo anchors the specific topic, "GenAI Creation," and its focused scope, "MVP Requirements." The vast, open red space to the left of the text represents the boundless potential of generative AI, while the structured, repeating arrow pattern on the right symbolizes the systematic, iterative process of development and the logical constraints of defining a Minimum Viable Product. The layout forces a relationship where creative possibility (open space) is channeled through a defined, directional process (arrow grid).

THE GESTALT IMPRESSION (The "Effect"): The overall impression is one of focused, authoritative innovation. The slide feels both expansive and disciplined, suggesting that while the subject of GenAI is vast, Adobe's approach is structured and purposeful. The viewer is guided to conclude that this presentation will be a clear, professional, and technically grounded discussion on a cutting-edge topic, framed within a well-defined project scope.

THE VISUAL SCAFFOLD (The "What"): The slide employs a minimalist, two-part layout against a solid, vibrant red background. The left quadrant contains the primary focal point: the white Adobe logo and two lines of sans-serif text, vertically stacked. The right third of the slide features a decorative grid of small, white, repeating arrow-like symbols, creating a subtle texture and visual interest that contrasts with the negative space on the left.

THE SEMANTIC BRIDGE (The "So What?"): The tabular layout creates a direct, causal relationship between project phases, their descriptions, success metrics (Goals), and timelines. The vertical stacking of 'Beta' and 'GA' (General Availability) represents a clear progression from a testing stage to a full release. The detailed bullet points under 'Description' and 'Goal' for the Beta phase contrast sharply with the sparse content for the GA phase, visually representing that Beta is the immediate, well-defined priority, while GA is a future, less-defined stage. The asterisk on 'Proposed Dates' and the footer note explicitly manage expectations, framing the timeline as provisional.

THE GESTALT IMPRESSION (The "Effect"): The slide projects an organized, analytical, and transparent vibe. It communicates that the project is structured and goal-oriented, with clear definitions of success for the upcoming phase. The audience is guided to conclude that the plan is well-thought-out but also flexible, acknowledging that firm dates are pending further estimation. This builds confidence in the process while maintaining realistic expectations about the timeline.

THE VISUAL SCAFFOLD (The "What"): The slide uses a four-column, two-row table as its primary structure, set against a clean white background. A strong horizontal axis is established by the dark teal header, which draws the eye from left to right across 'Key Phase', 'Description', 'Goal', and 'Proposed Dates'. The content is organized in a top-to-bottom reading flow, starting with the 'Beta' phase. The color palette is minimal, using red for the main title to signify importance, teal for structure, and black text for details.

THE SEMANTIC BRIDGE (The "So What?"): The slide's tabular structure bridges high-level product goals with granular feature requirements, creating a clear line of sight from strategy to execution. The left-most 'Key area' column, with its explicit 'Goal(s)', represents the user-centric vision (e.g., 'Understand user's end goal'). This vision is then systematically broken down into actionable 'Sub-area' and specific 'Requirement' columns. The bolded text within the requirements acts as a visual anchor, highlighting the core capabilities that directly fulfill the stated goals, ensuring that every technical detail is justified by a user need. This layout forces a logical cascade, demonstrating a rigorous, top-down product development methodology.

THE GESTALT IMPRESSION (The "Effect"): The overall impression is analytical, exhaustive, and authoritative. The dense, structured information conveys a sense of meticulous planning and technical competence. The audience is guided to the conclusion that the 'MVP requirements' are not arbitrary but are the result of a comprehensive and well-defined process. The slide feels like a definitive specification document, leaving little room for ambiguity and instilling confidence in the project's direction and scope.

THE VISUAL SCAFFOLD (The "What"): The slide employs a strict three-column tabular layout under a prominent title. A dark teal header row establishes the hierarchy: 'Key area', 'Sub-area', and 'Requirement'. The content flows vertically, with alternating light grey and white rows (zebra striping) enhancing readability across the dense grid. The first column uses bolding for category titles and bullet points for goals, while the third column uses bolding to emphasize key verbs and concepts within the requirement text. The color palette is professional and restrained, dominated by teal, greys, and black.

THE SEMANTIC BRIDGE (The "So What?"): The slide's three-column table structure logically bridges high-level product goals with granular technical requirements. The left column, 'Key area,' establishes the two primary pillars of user value: 'Iteration & editing' and 'Performance & quality.' These abstract concepts are then broken down into specific 'Sub-areas' (e.g., 'AI-Iterations,' 'Quality') and finally grounded in concrete, measurable 'Requirements' with bolded keywords acting as signposts. This hierarchical layout forces the viewer to understand that broad user goals are directly dependent on the successful implementation of detailed technical specifications, creating a clear line of sight from strategy to execution.

THE GESTALT IMPRESSION (The "Effect"): The overall impression is analytical, exhaustive, and authoritative. The dense, structured data and specific metrics (e.g., '90%+ accuracy,' 'P90 goal <15 seconds') project a sense of rigorous planning and technical competence. The audience is guided to the conclusion that this project is not a vague concept but a well-defined engineering challenge with clear, non-negotiable success criteria. The tone is internally focused, prioritizing clarity and accountability for a technical or product development team.

THE VISUAL SCAFFOLD (The "What"): The visual framework is a dominant three-column table that organizes information hierarchically from left to right. The layout uses horizontal banding with alternating shades of grey to aid row tracking and group related sub-areas. A strong red title bar establishes the slide's topic, while a dark blue header row defines the table's categories. Typographic emphasis (bolding) is used strategically within the 'Requirement' column to draw attention to key actions and metrics, guiding the viewer's scan through the dense text.

THE SEMANTIC BRIDGE (The "So What?"): The slide uses a stark visual metaphor, "Below the line," to create a clear hierarchy of priorities for a Minimum Viable Product (MVP). The upper table represents non-negotiable, core functionalities essential for the beta launch, while the lower table represents desirable but deferrable features. This layout forces a logical separation, communicating that the 'Last mile' and 'Discovery' are foundational pillars, whereas 'Outline generation' and 'Iteration' are secondary enhancements. The bolded text within each requirement acts as a micro-focal point, summarizing the key action or user benefit for quick comprehension.

THE GESTALT IMPRESSION (The "Effect"): The overall impression is authoritative, structured, and decisive. The slide projects a sense of clear-headed project management and strategic prioritization. The audience is guided to the conclusion that there is a well-defined, phased plan, with a clear distinction between 'must-haves' for the initial release and 'nice-to-haves' for future development. It feels like a definitive roadmap, not a brainstorming session.

THE VISUAL SCAFFOLD (The "What"): The slide employs a bisected, tabular layout, separating content into two distinct tables. A prominent red headline, "Below the line," serves as the primary visual divider. Each table uses a three-column structure ('Key area', 'Sub-area', 'Requirement') with a dark teal header for clear categorization. The color palette is minimal and corporate, using teal, grey, black, and a single red accent to create a clean, professional aesthetic. The structure guides the viewer through a top-to-bottom scan, reinforcing the priority sequence.

table_cells.text:
User intent gathering
Goal(s):
Understand user's end goal
Ability for user to provide goal and key parameters that will affect output e.g. audience, length etc
Ability to provide one or more source files (PDF, PPT, Excel, Word doc), URL, Free text, Transcript, Scans)
Help users generate only with a goal and no source content
Provide contextually relevant suggested prompts (using source doc) or sample suggested prompts (without source doc)
Auto-complete prompts based on source(s) and what user has already written

Outline & output generation

Goal(s):
Provide an effective storyline
High visual quality w.r.t. templates, layouts, images & icons
Comprehensive & relevant output
Help users understand that outline reflects overall storyline and the slide level topics which will be detailed out.

Support generation in following layouts: Title, Agenda, Content as list, Image + Text, Multi-column (text, images & icons), Stats, Grids, Timeline, Table (table + list) – with 20 17 templates with high relevance, visual fidelity & fit (scaling to a commonly aligned max content volume), & smart-cropping for images.
Ensure a variety among the 20 17 templates based on different design aesthetics; user should be able to select which one to apply
Optimize layout selection based on slide context  and generate content to best fit the recommended layout
Stock images and icons should be relevant and of high visual quality without watermarks or pixellations; a user should not encounter the Adobe stock upsell flow
Intelligently crop Image  to fit in template and image area after cropping, should be relevant for 80% of images in a presentation
Ensure a mix of slides w.r.t. stock images and icons to avoid visual repetition and offer variation

Icons should have same visual style language as the template and all icons on a slide should appear to have similar style i.e. line 
weight, color scheme, background transparency, aspect ratio.
Update Agenda slide to reflect key themes covered in the deck vs title of each slide

table_cells.text: MVP requirements - Beta on Acrobat Web (2/3)

grid.text: MVP requirements - Beta on Acrobat Web (2/3)

table_cells.text:
Iteration & editing

Goal(s):
Iterate first output to get closer to end goal
Flexibility to modify all aspects of generation

1. Support following AI edits:
a)  Add/modify slide via AI  or delete a slide.
b)  Add/delete/modify a slide via outline 
c) Regenerate the entire presentation by modifying prompt/goal, sources (will have an option to regenerate entire presentation or continue as is), audience/length/details etc levers. 
d) Select individual content on slide and change level of details (add details or simplify) or make concise; for images, offer ability to regenerate via prompt, see similar images or manuall replace
e) Change level of details (add details or simplify) at individual slide level and make entire slide concise
Enable theme application to modify color scheme and fonts within a template. Use the subset of themes created for documents/presentations
Support relevant manual edits for presentation use case following Express UI patterns.
Update undo/redo stack to support AI changes. (Single undo operation should undo both the change on the output slide as well as associated change in outline)

Performance & quality

Goal(s):
Highly relevant, accurate, comprehensive outline, text & image/icon generation adhering to user intent
Performant experience getting users from input to output stage in a couple of minutes
Ensure intent adherence in outline and output generation
Ensure the generated text and visual content (source & stock images + icons) meets the user intent with 90%+ accuracy & relevance
Image quality evaluation for relevance and quality Goal - highest relevance vs landscape and 80% of images/icons do not need to be updated by the user
Ensure icons are relevant. Goal - highest relevance vs landscape and 80% of icons do not need to be changed or have their styling edited
Overall output content (image + text) and visual appeal goal is to have 9/10 rating it best vs landscape
Ingestion performance P90 target should be <15 seconds for <10 pages and <0.5MBand <40 sec for 10-50 pages and <10MB
P90 goal for outline generation should <10 seconds for a 10 slide outline (medium length)
P90 goal for output generation & showing to the user should be <50 seconds for a 10 slide output. Includes the time to load the SDK and render output.
P90 goal for regenerating a slide after making sectional modification should be <20 seconds (aspirational goal <15sec)
P90 goal for regenerating selected content on a slide should be ~5-7 seconds

Provide ability to provide one or more source files (PDF, PPT, Excel, Word doc), URL, Free text, Transcript, Scans
Auto-fill key parameters like  length, audience etc. based on user prompt & sources (Lower Priority)
Starting with or without source document
Help users generate only with a goal (no source content) as well as with source content (files, URL, free text, outline)
Provide contextually relevant suggested prompts if user begins with source doc or if user doesn’t have sources provide helpful suggested prompts to help user craft their own
Auto-complete prompts based on source(s) and what user has already written
Rationalize outline to ensure users understand that outline reflects overall storyline and the slide level topics which will be detailed out.

Ensure a variety among the templates based on different design aesthetics.
Optimize layout selection and prioritization utilizing LLMs and generate content that will fit in the recommended layout
Stock images and icons should be of high visual quality without watermarks or pixellations and a user should not encounter the Adobe stock upsell flow

Ensure a balance of slides w.r.t. stock images and icons e.g. there should not be a case where all 3-column slides have icons

Icons should have same visual style language as the template and all icons on a slide should appear to have similar style i.e. line 
weight, color scheme, background transparency, aspect ratio.

c) Offer ability to add/delete/modify a slide via outline 
d) Allow users to change level of details (add details or simplify) at individual slide level and make entire slide concise
